title: Good: walk.rs Option<&mut Vec> nullification model is the correct JS-semantic mapping
description: mime-tree/src/walk.rs: the RFC 8621 §4.1.4 algorithm is specified in JavaScript using null re-assignment to 'close' an accumulator pointer. The Rust translation using &mut Option<&mut Vec<String>> with as_deref_mut() to create non-propagating child locals correctly models this semantics: a callee setting the Option to None does not affect the caller's Option. This is the right choice — a simpler approach (passing &mut Vec directly) would require a different mechanism to express 'stop adding to this list' without returning a bool, and would make the algorithm harder to compare to the RFC pseudocode. Worth defending if someone suggests simplifying.
close_reason: Positive review finding — design decision worth defending. No change needed.
